findings.text: Outside the node's declared write scope: prompt.txt:137-145 fences seven paths and does not grant this file or tests/standard_names/test_graph_edge_writers.py:360, yet both are rewritten in the diff. The edits are necessary (the old assertions pin the domain write this node removes, and leaving them adds three failure ids), so the repair is a coordinator scope extension, not a revert; until it is granted the record check refuses the run on changed_paths.

The successor's domain write is gated on isinstance(gc, GraphClient), so any caller-supplied client that is a proxy, subclass or wrapper — the shape services injection exists to allow — silently skips physics_domain, source_domains and the HAS_PHYSICS_DOMAIN edges, logging only at debug level; production currently reaches it with a real GraphClient so nothing is lost today.

physics_domain and source_domains are still passed as Cypher parameters to two statements (line 1036 and line 1281) whose SET clauses this commit removed; no query in the module references $physics_domain or $source_domains any more, so the values are computed and discarded and a reader cannot tell the parameters are dead without grepping the Cypher.

The base arm's header records '# module' as the worktree's graph_catalog.py rather than the base-tree module it imported; the arm's own result contradicts it — base-tree's test_has_physics_domain_edge_emitted and test_physics_domain_uses_coalesce pass, which head code would fail, and 73 failed/8409 passed is head's 8410 minus only the one added non-graph test — so the measurement stands but its recorded provenance does not.
